I work for the acquired company Viant. While I don't know all of the details this merger will eventually bring, one thing I can say is the media response to this is only using Myspace as the buzzword to garner interest. While it is true the data is a is a big part of this, it isn't all of the story. For those that think Myspace data is no longer relevant you're not taking into account that most people still use the same email address, their birthday and gender never change and geographical location is probably mostly still current. All of that is great information to have for better targeting ads. Print media is dying and Time, Inc was looking for a way into the digital advertising world; Viant is that way in. We've been told we are going to continue to operate as an independent subsidiary, which will be great if that's true. Viant wins with the new ingest of fresh and up to date user data Time, Inc brings to the table and Time wins by getting to monetize that same data that has been theoretically "sitting on their shelf".
